results.correct_value: ACCESS describes only Half Moon Crag (roadside pullout on Tye Road near Wellington, west of Stevens Pass); the Mount Index / Lake Serene sentences are removed.
results.evidence: Half Moon Crag is a short-route granite crag reached from Tye Road (old Stevens Pass Highway) ~1.4 mi from US-2 near Wellington, just west of Stevens Pass; Mount Index and the Lake Serene trailhead are ~25 mi west near Index. The Mount Index sentences in access.notes and access.parking_pass are copied text about another objective; removing them leaves the crag-specific sentences intact.

results.fact: Whether trailhead parking requires a fee/pass
results.evidence: The nearby Wellington Trailhead (2.8 mi up the Old Stevens Pass Highway, on FS Rd 050) is a Forest Service fee site requiring a Recreation Pass or $5/day, but the crag's parking is an unofficial roadside pullout ~1.4 mi from US-2, which is not that trailhead. No source states whether a pass is needed at this pullout; the Northwest Forest Pass applies at standard-amenity fee sites, suggesting none, but that is inference, not a second agreeing source. After the Mount Index removal, access.notes/parking_pass say no fee site while access.passRequired says 'Recreation pass' — left open.

results.fact: Rappel distance vs route length
results.evidence: The route's own climbing-database page gives its height as 50 ft (15 m), matching length_m, and the crag-wide description says all routes are about 85 ft or less — so the 85-ft figure in descent_text looks like the crag cap reused. Only one external source gives the per-route height and only one row field agrees, so no rewrite was made; suggested fix is to drop the 85-ft figure from descent_text.

results.fact: Permit field names the Wild Sky Wilderness
results.evidence: `permit` says 'Free self-issue Wild Sky Wilderness permit...', while access.permit is 'N/A' and climbing_permit_required is false. Wild Sky Wilderness lies along the North Fork Skykomish and Beckler rivers, well west of Wellington, so the Wild Sky wording appears copied from the Mount Index text; but whether the crag falls inside the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness (just north of Stevens Pass) could not be confirmed by two sources, so the correct permit statement is not settled. Same on all five Half Moon Crag routes.
